what_its_for: Rasagiline is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It helps reduce symptoms like tremors, stiffness, and slowness of movement. It can be used alone in early Parkinson's disease or together with other Parkinson's medicines like levodopa.
how_to_take: Take rasagiline by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 1 mg once daily depending on how well your symptoms are controlled and how you tolerate the medicine. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. Taking a double dose can increase your risk of serious side effects.
storage: Store rasagiline at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of foods high in tyramine, such as aged cheeses, cured or smoked meats, pickled foods, sauerkraut, soy sauce, tap beer, and red wine, as this can cause a dangerous rise in blood pressure. Do not take antidepressants (especially SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, or St. John's Wort), other MAO inhibitors, meperidine (Demerol), tramadol, methadone, or certain cold medicines containing dextromethorphan without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist. Avoid alcohol. Use caution when driving or operating machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause drowsiness or dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a severe headache, stiff neck, fast or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, sudden sweating, nausea or vomiting, or vision changes (these may be signs of a dangerous rise in blood pressure called hypertensive crisis). Also call your doctor if you notice: unusual urges such as gambling, overeating, or sexual urges; hallucinations or confusion; skin changes or new moles (rasagiline may increase the risk of skin cancer); fainting or falling; worsening of involuntary movements if you also take levodopa; or any signs of allergic reaction such as rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your Parkinson's symptoms within a few weeks of starting rasagiline. However, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well, as Parkinson's disease is a long-term condition that requires ongoing treatment.
special_populations: Liver problems: If you have mild liver disease, your doctor will keep your dose at 0.5 mg once daily. Rasagiline is NOT recommended if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Elderly patients: Older adults can take rasagiline, but your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects like dizziness and falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of rasagiline during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Children: Rasagiline is not approved for use in children.
